items.title: 60499_Garvin Bushell oral history interview
items.q: I remember distinctly a lady came to Springfield... I've heard that she became the wife of Teddy Wilson, who taught Teddy Wilson how to play piano.

ctx.x: Yes, Indiana. Yes, because I remember distinctly a lady came to Springfield -- her first name was Irene. A very fine pianist -- this was about 1910 or 11 and since then I've heard that she became the wife of Teddy Wilson, who taught Teddy Wilson how to play piano. She came out of Indiana, out of Indianapolis. And it seems as though ragtime was just the major thing to have for your parties and the new tunes as they came out -- Springfield had them.
